S: Cher on Amber: from far away it's OK, up close it's a big old mess

Heirloom tomatoes, torn burrata, basil oil and balsamic with chargrilled sourdough. Blend half the basil with 60ml of the olive oil and a pinch of salt for the basil oil. Cut the tomatoes into wedges and rounds, salt them and leave for 10 minutes. Slice the sourdough, brush with the rest of the oil and toast in a hot grill pan until charred, then rub with the cut garlic. Lay the tomatoes on a platter, tear the burrata over, spoon on the basil oil and balsamic and scatter the rest of the basil. Serve with the toast.
Lime guacamole and fresh tomato salsa with a bag of corn chips

Corn chips with guacamole (avocado mashed with lime, onion, coriander and chilli) and a fresh salsa of diced tomato, onion and lime. Mash 3 avocados with the juice of 2 limes, finely chopped onion, coriander and a little chilli. Dice 3 tomatoes with onion and lime juice for salsa. Serve both with a 300g bag of corn chips.
Warm soft pretzels rolled in cinnamon sugar, with a sweet cream cheese dip
Soft pretzels brushed with melted butter, rolled in cinnamon sugar, warmed at 200C for 5 minutes, with a cream cheese icing dip.
Pan fried pork and cabbage dumplings with ginger, steamed until tender

Pork and cabbage potstickers folded, fried until the bottoms brown, steamed under a lid, with a soy and black vinegar dip. Mix 400g pork mince with 2 cups shredded wombok, salted and squeezed, and 1 tbsp grated ginger. Fill 30 gyoza wrappers and pleat. Fry until browned, add water and steam under a lid for 4 minutes. Dip in soy and Chinkiang vinegar.
Corn chips baked with black beans, cheddar and jalapeños

Corn chips layered with black beans, cheddar and jalapeño, baked at 200C for 8 minutes (the oven, not the microwave), salsa and sour cream. Layer a 300g bag of corn chips with a drained tin of black beans, 200g grated cheddar and sliced jalapeños. Bake in the oven at 200C for 8 minutes, not the microwave. Top with diced tomato and 150g sour cream.
the gremlin that drinks the vegetable serum in the Splice O' Life lab and sprouts leaves

Rice paper rolls of mint, coriander, cos, cucumber, carrot and vermicelli with a peanut hoisin dip. Soak the vermicelli in just-boiled water for 5 minutes, drain and cool under the tap. Cut the cucumber and carrots into thin sticks and pick the herbs and lettuce leaves. Dip a rice paper sheet in warm water for a few seconds and lay it flat. Fill with lettuce, noodles, vegetables and herbs, fold in the sides and roll up tight. Repeat. Whisk the hoisin, peanut butter, lime juice and 3 tbsp warm water, scatter with chopped peanuts and serve with the rolls.
Crisp bacon in buttered soft rolls with brown sauce, wrapped to stay warm
Thick bacon rashers fried crisp, stuffed into soft white rolls with butter and brown sauce, wrapped in paper for the next drop.
Mussels steamed in white wine, garlic and butter, with parsley and crusty bread
Mussels steamed open in white wine with garlic, eschalot and parsley, finished with butter, served with crusty bread to mop up.
the same breakfast on the same base, every single morning

Vintage cheddar, mustard and smoked paprika bubbled on thick toast. Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk until thick. Take off the heat and stir in the cheddar, mustard, paprika and egg yolk. Toast the bread on one side under a hot grill, spread the cheese mix on the other side and grill for 4 minutes until bubbling and browned in spots. Cut into fingers and scatter with sliced spring onion.
M: Farmhouse beef and mushroom stew with mash
the farmhouse where Cage and Rita hide out

Beef chuck braised slowly with mushrooms, carrots and thyme over buttery mash. Toss the beef in the flour with salt and pepper and brown it in batches in the oil in a heavy pot. Fry the chopped onion, carrots, mushrooms and garlic for 5 minutes, stir in the tomato paste, then add the stock and thyme and put the beef back in. Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours until the beef is tender. Boil the peeled potatoes for 20 minutes, drain and mash with the butter and milk. Serve the stew over the mash.
Angel of Verdun chicken, cider and cream
Chicken thighs and mushrooms simmered in apple cider and cream, with baguette

Chicken thighs browned and braised in apple cider with eschalots and mushrooms, finished with cream and parsley, with a warm baguette to mop the sauce. Season 1kg chicken thighs and brown in butter for 4 minutes a side, then set aside. Soften 2 sliced eschalots and 200g sliced mushrooms in the pan. Pour in 375ml apple cider and scrape up the browned bits. Return the chicken, cover and simmer 25 minutes. Stir in 150ml cream and simmer 3 minutes until glossy. Scatter with parsley and serve with a warm baguette.
Russell, the kid in the Ice Box with fire for fists

Charred peri peri chicken thighs with turmeric rice and a crunchy slaw. Blitz the chillies, garlic, juice of 1 lemon, paprika, vinegar, 3 tbsp of the oil and a pinch of salt. Toss with the chicken and leave for 20 minutes. Simmer the rice with the turmeric and 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5. Cook the chicken in a hot grill pan with the rest of the oil for 5 minutes a side until charred and cooked through. Shred the cabbage and grate the carrots, then toss with the mayonnaise and a squeeze of the other lemon. Slice the chicken and serve over the rice with the slaw.
Seared sirloin in a red wine pan sauce, oven chips

Steaks seared and butter basted, sliced with chips and a red wine sauce, candles on the table. Cut 1kg potatoes into chips and roast until crisp. Sear 4 sirloin steaks in a very hot pan, add butter and baste for a minute, then rest. Add 150ml red wine and 250ml beef stock to the pan and reduce until glossy. Slice and serve by candlelight.

S: Warm sourdough with salted butter and oil with dukkah
Warm a sourdough loaf at 200C for 8 minutes and tear into chunks. Serve with 125g soft salted butter and a shallow dish of extra virgin olive oil with 3 tbsp dukkah scattered on top for dipping.
Goodspeed's little green glass beads, the ones nobody can drop

Crisp risotto balls of pea, mint and parmesan with a mozzarella middle and lemon mayo. Soften the chopped onion in the butter, stir in the rice, then add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes until thick. Blitz the peas with half the mint and stir through the risotto with the parmesan. Spread on a tray. Chill for 1 hour until firm. Roll into 16 balls with a cube of mozzarella in each. Roll in flour, then beaten egg, then panko. Heat the oil to 180C and fry in batches for 4 minutes until golden. Drain on paper towel. Mix the mayonnaise with the lemon zest and juice and the rest of the mint, chopped, and serve with the arancini.
Prawns tossed in hot olive oil with garlic, chilli and butter
Prawns sautéed hot in olive oil with sliced garlic and chilli, finished with butter, white wine and parsley, sourdough for the pan juices.
M: San Francisco cioppino and garlic toast
the city's own seafood stew, across the bay from the Rock

Fennel, garlic and chilli simmered in tomato and white wine with prawns, mussels, clams and snapper, served with charred garlic sourdough. Soften 1 sliced fennel bulb, 1 onion and 4 garlic cloves in olive oil with a pinch of chilli flakes. Add 250ml white wine, 400g crushed tomatoes and 500ml fish stock and simmer 20 minutes. Add 500g clams and 500g mussels, cover 3 minutes, then 400g snapper chunks and 12 green prawns for 4 minutes more until everything is cooked. Finish with parsley. Grill thick sourdough slices rubbed with garlic and olive oil.
Butter-basted rib eye with béarnaise and frites

Reduce 60ml white wine vinegar with tarragon to 2 tbsp, whisk with 3 yolks over low heat and drizzle in 200g warm clarified butter. Fry 1kg potato chips twice. Sear 4 rib eyes, baste with 40g butter, thyme and garlic, rest and serve.

S: Prunes stuffed with blue cheese, wrapped in bacon and baked crisp
Prunes stuffed with blue cheese, wrapped in streaky bacon and baked crisp, a Jazz Age party classic.
Velma's All That Jazz at the Onyx Club, the night it all starts

Oysters baked under spinach, parsley, butter and parmesan crumbs. Heat the oven grill to high. Wilt the spinach in a dry pan, squeeze it out and chop finely with the parsley and spring onions. Mash into the butter with the breadcrumbs, parmesan, a squeeze of lemon and a few drops of hot sauce. Sit the oysters on a tray of rock salt, top each with the spinach butter and grill for 4 minutes until bubbling and golden. Serve with lemon wedges.
Twisted puff pastry strips with parmesan and paprika
Puff pastry brushed with egg, covered in grated parmesan and paprika, cut into thin strips like cell bars, twisted, baked at 200C for 12 minutes.

M: Beef and pork meatloaf with a tomato glaze
Beef and pork mince with breadcrumbs, egg, onion and Worcestershire, shaped in a tin, glazed with tomato sauce and brown sugar, baked at 180C for an hour. Mash.
Hightower, the cadet who tips a car over by hand

Crumbed chicken breast under napoli and melted mozzarella, with chips and a rocket salad. Simmer the tomatoes with the crushed garlic, oregano and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes until thick. Slice each breast in half through the middle and flatten. Dip in flour, then beaten egg, then panko. Bake the chips at 220C for 25 minutes. Shallow fry the chicken in the vegetable oil for 3 minutes a side until golden. Spoon the napoli over the chicken, cover with mozzarella and grill for 5 minutes until bubbling. Dress the rocket with the olive oil and lemon and serve with the parmigiana and chips.
Whole roast chicken stuffed with lemon, garlic and thyme

Whole chicken roasted over lemon, garlic and thyme until the skin crackles, with crispy potatoes, roast carrots and a punchy pan gravy. Heat the oven to 200C. Rub a 1.8kg chicken with 30g soft butter, salt and pepper and stuff with 1 halved lemon, 4 garlic cloves and thyme. Toss 1kg potatoes and 4 carrots in chunks with oil and salt around it. Roast 1 hour 15 minutes, turning the vegetables once. Rest the chicken 10 minutes. Whisk 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices, add 300ml stock and simmer 3 minutes for gravy.
Mooj, full of advice nobody asked for

Lamb shoulder slow cooked with Kashmiri chilli, yoghurt and whole spices, with basmati rice and cucumber raita. Fry the sliced onions in the ghee for 12 minutes until deep golden, then add the grated garlic and ginger, chilli, garam masala and cardamom for 1 minute. Add the lamb and brown on all sides, then stir in the tomatoes, 100g of the yoghurt and 250ml water. Cover and simmer gently for 1 and a half hours until the lamb is tender. Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5. Grate the cucumber, squeeze it out and mix with the rest of the yoghurt and a pinch of salt. Scatter the curry with coriander and serve with the rice and raita.
Glazed beef meatloaf baked in a loaf tin

A hearty beef meatloaf with a tangy tomato glaze, sliced thick and served with buttery mash, peas and a rich brown onion gravy. Mix 800g beef mince, 1 grated onion, 1 egg, 60g breadcrumbs, 2 tsp Worcestershire and salt. Press into a lined loaf tin and spread with 4 tbsp tomato sauce mixed with 1 tbsp brown sugar. Bake at 180C for 1 hour. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and milk. Fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes, stir in 1 tbsp flour, then 400ml beef stock and simmer to a gravy. Serve with 300g peas.
the EM-50 run over the border into Czechoslovakia

Chicken thighs braised in sweet paprika and sour cream with buttered egg noodles and cucumber salad. Brown the chicken in half the butter and set aside. Fry the sliced onions and capsicum in the same pan for 6 minutes, then stir in the paprika and flour for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, stock and chicken and simmer for 30 minutes until tender. Thinly slice the cucumbers and toss with the vinegar, a pinch of sugar and half the dill. Cook the noodles, drain and toss with the rest of the butter. Stir the sour cream through the chicken off the heat, scatter with dill and serve with the noodles and cucumber salad.
Claus family honey mustard glazed ham
Clove studded leg ham glazed with honey and Dijon mustard

A leg ham scored and glazed with honey, mustard and orange until sticky and caramelised, served with roast potatoes and buttery greens. Remove the rind from a 2.5kg half leg ham, score the fat in a diamond pattern and stud with cloves. Simmer 120ml honey, 3 tbsp Dijon mustard, 60g brown sugar and the juice of 1 orange for 3 minutes. Bake the ham at 180C for 45 minutes, brushing with glaze every 15 minutes. Roast 1kg halved potatoes in oil alongside. Toss 300g green beans and broccolini in butter. Slice the ham thickly to serve.
Fred's support group for famous people's brothers

Chicken, leek and peas in a creamy thyme sauce under a puff pastry lid. Brown the diced chicken in half the butter, then add the sliced leeks, diced carrots and the rest of the butter and cook for 6 minutes. Stir in the flour, then the stock, cream and thyme leaves and simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Stir in the peas. Heat the oven to 200C. Spoon the filling into a pie dish and cover with the pastry, pressing the edges. Brush with beaten egg, cut a steam hole and bake for 30 minutes until puffed and golden.
Roast chicken with sage and lemon breadcrumb stuffing

Roast chicken with bread and herb stuffing, crunchy roast potatoes, glazed carrots and gravy, a small Christmas dinner done properly. Fry 1 diced onion in 40g butter, mix with 150g fresh breadcrumbs, 2 tbsp chopped sage, the zest of 1 lemon and 1 egg, and stuff a 1.8kg chicken. Rub with butter and salt and roast at 200C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Roast 1kg halved potatoes in oil for 50 minutes. Glaze 4 carrots with 20g butter and 1 tbsp honey. Rest the chicken, then make gravy from the juices with 1 tbsp flour and 350ml stock.
Mary cooks for the three left behind

Chuck roast braised for hours with carrots, onions and potatoes in its own gravy. Heat the oven to 160C. Season the beef well and brown all over in the oil in a heavy pot. Lift out. Fry the onion wedges and garlic for 5 minutes, stir in the tomato paste, then add the stock, Worcestershire and thyme. Put the beef back, cover and braise in the oven for 2 hours. Add the carrots and halved potatoes and braise for 1 more hour until everything is tender. Lift out the beef and vegetables, thicken the juices with the cornflour mixed with a little water and simmer for 2 minutes. Slice the beef and serve with the vegetables, gravy and chopped parsley.
Buttermilk fried chicken, mashed potato, pepper gravy and chilli honey

Buttermilk brined chicken fried crisp and golden, with creamy mash, peppery white gravy and hot honey on the side. Soak 1.2kg chicken pieces in 400ml buttermilk with 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp hot sauce for at least 2 hours. Toss in 200g plain flour mixed with 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder and salt. Fry at 165C for 12 to 15 minutes until golden and cooked through. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with butter and milk. Make gravy with 30g butter, 2 tbsp flour, 400ml milk and lots of pepper. Warm 3 tbsp honey with chilli flakes.
Sunshine, the new kid from California

Chilli lime grilled fish in warm corn tortillas with cabbage slaw, avocado and lime crema. Rub the fish with the chilli, cumin, the juice of 1 lime, the oil and a pinch of salt. Shred the cabbage and toss with the juice of 1 lime, chopped coriander and sliced jalapeño. Mix the sour cream with the zest and juice of the last lime. Cook the fish in a hot grill pan for 3 minutes a side, then break into chunks. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill with fish, slaw, sliced avocado and crema.
Slow-cooked chuck roast with carrots, potatoes and horseradish sour cream

Chuck roast braised low and slow with onions, carrots and potatoes in a rich gravy, served with horseradish cream and crusty bread. Season a 1.5kg chuck roast and brown all over in 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pot. Add 2 quartered onions, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 500ml beef stock, 1 tbsp Worcestershire, thyme and 2 bay leaves. Cover and cook at 160C for 2 hours. Add 4 carrots and 800g halved potatoes and cook 1 hour more. Thicken the juices with 1 tbsp cornflour. Mix 150g sour cream with 2 tbsp horseradish cream.
Friday nights at Holy Cross, waiting on Notre Dame

Beer-battered flathead, thick chips, tartare and a cabbage slaw. Bake the chips at 220C for 25 minutes. Mix the mayonnaise with chopped capers, gherkins and a squeeze of lemon for the tartare. Toss the shredded cabbage and grated carrot with 2 tbsp of it. Whisk 120g of the flour with the baking powder and lager until smooth. Heat the oil to 180C. Dust the fish in the rest of the flour, dip in the batter and fry in batches for 4 minutes until golden. Serve with the chips, tartare, slaw and lemon wedges.
Jackson's Star never-sunrise beef and barley stew
the colony never sees the sun, so dinner has to warm you instead

Toss 800g diced beef chuck in 2 tbsp flour and brown in batches in 2 tbsp oil. Soften 1 onion, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks and 2 garlic cloves, stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste, add 1.2 litres beef stock, 2 bay leaves and 1 tsp dried thyme and simmer covered for 1 hour. Add 100g pearl barley and simmer 40 minutes more. Season, scatter with parsley and serve with crusty bread.
hot food at last, aboard the drifting station

Panko chicken with a sweet Japanese curry sauce, steamed rice and pickled cucumber. Fry the chopped onion and carrots in 1 tbsp of the oil for 8 minutes, stir in 2 tbsp of the flour and the curry powder, then add the stock, soy and honey and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend smooth. Simmer the rice with 450ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5. Slice the cucumber thinly and toss with the rice vinegar and a pinch of sugar. Slice each breast in half through the middle. Dip in the rest of the flour, then beaten egg, then panko. Shallow fry in the rest of the oil for 3 minutes a side until golden, then slice. Serve the chicken over rice with the curry sauce poured alongside and the cucumber.
the hot meal on the cafeteria line at Haddonfield Memorial
Chicken, carrot, celery and peas in a creamy thyme sauce under a golden puff pastry lid.
the security guard's supper at the front desk

Pork and beef meatballs simmered in tomato sauce, in toasted rolls under melted provolone. Mix the mince, breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan, 1 crushed garlic clove and salt, and roll into 20 meatballs. Brown the meatballs in the oil and lift out. Fry the rest of the garlic for 1 minute, add the passata and oregano, put the meatballs back and simmer for 20 minutes. Split and toast the rolls, fill with meatballs and sauce, lay over the provolone and grill for 2 minutes until melted. Tuck in the basil and serve with the rocket on the side.
Lager-battered flathead, slaw, chipotle crema in warm tortillas

Crisp beer-battered flathead in warm tortillas with lime slaw, pickled red onion, chipotle crema and fresh coriander. Slice 1 red onion and soak in the juice of 2 limes with a pinch of salt for 20 minutes. Whisk 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and 250ml cold lager to a batter. Cut 600g flathead fillets into strips, dip in batter and fry at 180C for 3 minutes. Toss half a shredded cabbage with lime juice and salt. Mix 150g sour cream with 1 tsp chipotle sauce. Fill 12 warm tortillas with slaw, fish, crema, onion and coriander.
spring break in Puerto Mexico, still on the job

Chargrilled lime and garlic skirt steak in big flour tortillas with rice, black beans, pico de gallo and sour cream. Rub the steak with the juice of 2 limes, crushed garlic, cumin, oil and salt and leave for 30 minutes. Simmer the rice with 400ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, rest for 5, then stir through the beans. Dice the tomatoes, onion and jalapeño and mix with chopped coriander and the last lime for the pico de gallo. Grill the steak very hot for 3 minutes a side, rest for 5 minutes and slice thin across the grain. Warm the tortillas, fill with rice and beans, steak, cheddar, pico de gallo and sour cream, and roll up tight.
D Company field kitchen beef and beans
Slow-cooked beef, cannellini beans and paprika over buttered rice

Chuck steak slow-cooked with smoky paprika, tomato and beans until tender, served with buttered rice and pickled chilli for a kick. Brown 800g diced chuck in batches in 2 tbsp oil. Add 1 diced onion, 2 garlic cloves and 1 diced capsicum and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp cumin, 400g tin crushed tomatoes, 400ml beef stock and a drained 400g tin cannellini beans. Cover and simmer 2 hours until tender. Cook 300g rice and stir through 20g butter. Serve with sliced pickled chilli.
three days' leave down at Vung Tau

Pork belly braised in dark caramel, fish sauce and coconut water with boiled eggs, jasmine rice and cucumber. Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool and peel. Cut the pork into 4cm pieces. Melt the sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat until dark amber, then stir in the sliced shallots and garlic. Add the pork and toss for 5 minutes, then add the fish sauce and coconut water. Simmer gently, half covered, for 1 hour 15 minutes, adding the eggs for the last 20 minutes, until the pork is tender and the sauce sticky. Simmer the rice with 450ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5. Serve with the rice, sliced cucumber, spring onion and chilli.
Serge at the gallery desk, with the accent nobody can place

Grilled chicken, cos, parmesan, garlic croutons and a sharp anchovy dressing. Tear the bread into chunks, toss with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and 1 crushed garlic clove and bake at 200C for 10 minutes until golden. Blend the egg yolk, anchovies, the other garlic clove, mustard and lemon juice, then drizzle in the light olive oil until thick. Grate in half the parmesan. Slice the chicken in half through the middle, rub with the rest of the oil and salt and cook in a hot grill pan for 4 minutes a side. Rest and slice. Toss the cos leaves with the dressing and croutons, top with the chicken and shave over the rest of the parmesan.
the steak sandwich Axel puts on someone else's tab
Sirloin seared hard and sliced thin, caramelised onion, Swiss and horseradish mayo on a toasted brioche roll, fries on the side.

S: Granny Smith apples and cinnamon baked in a sweet shortcrust
Apple pie of Granny Smiths, sugar and cinnamon in a double crust, baked at 190C for 50 minutes, served in wedges with strong drip coffee.
Charlene on the balcony, letting Chris walk away

Chargrilled corn with lime mayo, cotija, chilli and coriander. Brush the corn with melted butter and cook in a very hot grill pan, turning, for 10 minutes until charred all over. Mix the mayonnaise with the zest and juice of 1 lime. Brush the hot corn with the lime mayo, roll in crumbled cotija, dust with chilli and scatter with coriander. Serve with lime wedges.
Fresh shucked oysters on ice with lemon and shallot mignonette
Freshly shucked oysters on ice with a shallot and red wine vinegar mignonette and lemon.
Johnny Storm's charred chicken shawarma bites
Flame on, right up until Cassandra gets her hands on him

Spiced charred chicken on warm flatbread with garlic sauce, pickles and parsley. Toss the chicken with the spice, lemon juice, oil and salt and leave for 15 minutes. Mix the yoghurt with the crushed garlic and a pinch of salt. Cook the chicken in a very hot grill pan for 4 minutes a side until charred, then slice. Warm the flatbreads, cut each into quarters and top with chicken, garlic sauce, pickles, diced tomato and parsley.
Fried tortilla rolls of beef, refried beans and cheese
Mini fried burritos filled with spiced beef, beans and cheese, with sour cream and salsa.
Paper thin fried potato chips tossed in smoked paprika and garlic powder
Potatoes sliced thin on a mandoline, fried at 170C until crisp, tossed straight away with smoked paprika, garlic powder and salt.

M: Poached eggs and hollandaise on toasted English muffins
Eggs poached 3 minutes, set on toasted English muffins with ham, covered in hollandaise of yolks whisked with melted butter and lemon.
Rehearsal dinner lemon roast chicken with green beans
yet another rehearsal dinner for Maggie, and the eggs debate at breakfast

Lemon and thyme roast chicken with crushed potatoes and garlicky green beans. Heat the oven to 200C. Rub the chicken with butter mixed with thyme leaves and salt and stuff it with a halved lemon and half the garlic. Roast the chicken for 1 hour 15 minutes with the halved potatoes tossed in oil around it, until the juices run clear. Rest the chicken for 15 minutes and crush the potatoes with a fork in the pan juices. Boil the beans for 4 minutes, drain and toss with the rest of the garlic, sliced and fried in a little oil, the almonds and the other lemon. Carve and serve with the potatoes and beans.
Chicken thigh and leek in creamy sauce under a puff pastry lid
Chicken and leek pot pie under puff pastry, the kind of dinner a careful man counts the bites of.
Hilbert, the literature professor who sits the lifeguard chair at the campus pool

Crisp-skin barramundi with lemon pepper butter, crushed potatoes and a green salad. Boil the potatoes for 18 minutes, drain and crush lightly with a fork and 1 tbsp of the oil. Mash the butter with the lemon zest, pepper and a pinch of salt. Score the fish skin, salt it and cook skin side down in the rest of the oil for 5 minutes until crisp, then flip for 2 minutes. Toss the leaves and sliced cucumber with the vinegar and a squeeze of lemon. Top the fish with the lemon pepper butter and serve with the potatoes and salad.
Capsicums stuffed with beef and rice, baked in tomato, garlic yoghurt

Red capsicums stuffed with paprika-spiced beef and rice, baked in a rich tomato sauce and served with garlic yoghurt and crusty bread. Fry 1 diced onion and 2 garlic cloves, add 500g beef mince and brown. Stir in 100g long grain rice, 2 tsp sweet paprika, 1 tsp smoked paprika, salt and 150ml water and cook 5 minutes. Cut the tops off 4 large red capsicums, remove the seeds and fill. Stand in a dish, pour around 700g passata mixed with 200ml water and bake covered at 180C for 50 minutes. Mix 200g Greek yoghurt with 1 crushed garlic clove.
Christmas dinner at the shelter where Tom volunteers, and Kate finally pitches in

Roast turkey breast with sage butter, roast potatoes, Brussels sprouts and gravy. Heat the oven to 190C. Mash the butter with chopped sage, lemon zest and salt and push it under the turkey skin. Roast the turkey for 1 hour 20 minutes, with the parboiled potatoes tossed in 2 tbsp of the oil in a second tray. Rest the turkey for 20 minutes. Halve the sprouts and roast them in the rest of the oil for 15 minutes. Stir the flour into the roasting pan juices on the stove, whisk in the stock and simmer for 4 minutes for gravy. Carve and serve with the potatoes, sprouts and gravy.
Sirloin steaks with garlic butter and crisp smashed potatoes

Pan-seared sirloin basted in garlic thyme butter, with crispy smashed potatoes, buttered greens and a red wine jus. Boil 800g baby potatoes for 15 minutes, drain, smash flat on a tray, drizzle with oil and roast at 220C for 30 minutes. Season 4 sirloin steaks and sear in a hot pan for 3 minutes a side. Add 50g butter, 2 crushed garlic cloves and thyme and baste for 1 minute. Rest the steaks. Add 150ml red wine and 150ml beef stock to the pan and reduce by half. Sauté 300g green beans in butter.
Edgar and Estelle, still holding hands after fifty-odd Valentine's Days

Crisp-skin salmon with lemon butter sauce, asparagus and kipfler potatoes. Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until tender, then halve them. Simmer the chopped shallot in the vinegar until almost gone, then whisk in the butter a piece at a time over low heat with a squeeze of lemon. Salt the salmon skin and cook skin side down in the oil for 5 minutes until crisp, then flip for 2 minutes. Blanch the asparagus for 2 minutes. Plate the salmon on the potatoes and asparagus, spoon over the sauce and scatter with chives.
Granny's cottage chicken and mushroom pot pie
Granny's cottage on the far side of the forest

Chicken thigh, leek, mushrooms and thyme in a creamy mustard sauce under a deep golden puff pastry lid. Season 800g diced boneless chicken thighs and brown in 30g butter and 1 tbsp oil in a large frying pan, then lift out. Soften 1 sliced leek, 250g halved button mushrooms, 2 crushed garlic cloves and the leaves from 3 thyme sprigs in the pan. Stir in 3 tbsp plain flour, then 400ml chicken stock, 150ml thickened cream and 1 tsp Dijon mustard. Return the chicken and simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Stir in 2 tbsp chopped parsley, season and spoon into a 2 litre pie dish, then cool for 10 minutes. Cover with 2 sheets of puff pastry, press the edges, brush with beaten egg, cut a steam hole and bake at 200C for 30 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
King's festival roast pork with apples
three nights of the King's festival, and Cinderella runs out of every one

Crackling pork loin roasted on apples and onions, with cider gravy and buttered greens. Heat the oven to 240C. Score the skin, rub with the salt and sit the pork on the quartered apples, onions and sage in a roasting tin. Roast for 30 minutes until the skin crackles, then turn down to 180C. Roast for 1 more hour, then rest for 15 minutes. Stir the flour into the pan juices on the stove, add the cider and simmer for 4 minutes for gravy. Boil the beans for 4 minutes, then toss with the spinach and butter until wilted. Carve and serve with the roast apples, gravy and greens.
Whoville roast beast with crispy potatoes
Garlic rosemary beef sirloin roast with crisp roast potatoes

Garlic and herb crusted roast beef carved at the table, with crunchy duck fat potatoes, honey roast carrots and a rich red gravy. Rub a 1.5kg beef sirloin roast with 2 crushed garlic cloves, chopped rosemary, oil and salt. Parboil 1.2kg quartered potatoes for 8 minutes, drain, rough up and toss in 3 tbsp duck fat. Roast the potatoes at 200C for 50 minutes and the beef for 50 minutes for medium rare, adding 4 carrots tossed in honey for the last 35. Rest the beef 15 minutes. Whisk 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices with 400ml beef stock to make gravy.
Donna Who's after-night-shift mac and cheese
Donna, working nights and raising three, the reason Cindy Lou writes to Santa

Baked macaroni in a three-cheese sauce under crunchy crumbs, with roast broccoli. Cook the macaroni for 2 minutes less than the packet says and drain. Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and simmer until thick. Stir in the cheddar, gruyère and mustard. Fold the macaroni through the sauce and tip into a baking dish. Top with the panko and parmesan. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden, with the broccoli florets tossed in the oil and salt on a second tray. Serve the mac and cheese with the broccoli.
between shows in Vietnam, a bowl from a street stall outside the base

Clear ginger and star anise chicken broth with rice noodles, herbs, bean sprouts and lime. Char the halved onion and ginger in a dry pan, then toast the star anise and cinnamon for 1 minute. Put the chicken, onion, ginger and spices in a pot with 2 litres of water and simmer gently for 50 minutes, skimming. Lift out the chicken and shred the meat. Strain the broth and season with the fish sauce and sugar. Soak or cook the noodles as the packet says and divide between bowls. Top with the chicken, pour over the hot broth and serve with bean sprouts, herbs, lime and chilli.
Topside roast with roast potatoes and pumpkin, peas and pan gravy
Beef topside seasoned and roasted at 200C to 52C, rested and carved thin, with roast potatoes and pumpkin, peas and a gravy made in the roasting tin with flour and stock.
Chicken thighs baked with 40 whole garlic cloves, thyme and white wine
Chicken thighs browned skin side down, forty unpeeled garlic cloves, thyme and white wine added, covered and baked at 180C for an hour. Squeeze the garlic onto crusty bread.
the club where Jerry dances with Amy, and she forgets everyone else

Seared sirloin sliced rare over rocket and shaved parmesan with balsamic and roast garlic potatoes. Halve the potatoes, toss with 2 tbsp of the oil, the bashed garlic cloves and rosemary and roast at 220C for 35 minutes. Rub the steaks with the rest of the oil and salt and sear in a very hot pan for 3 minutes a side for rare. Rest the steaks for 8 minutes, then slice thinly. Lay the steak over the rocket, shave over the parmesan, drizzle with balsamic and serve with the potatoes.
Style Boyz fish tacos with mango salsa
Chilli lime grilled fish in tortillas with fresh mango salsa

Chilli and lime grilled white fish in warm corn tortillas with fresh mango salsa, shredded cabbage, avocado crema and coriander. Rub 600g firm white fish fillets with 1 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp cumin, the zest of 1 lime and 1 tbsp oil. Grill 3 minutes a side and flake. Dice 1 mango, half a red onion and 1 red chilli and toss with lime juice and coriander. Blend 1 avocado with 100g sour cream and lime juice. Warm 12 small corn tortillas in a dry pan. Fill with shredded cabbage, fish, salsa and crema.
Lawrence's Colorado farm steak with chimichurri
Lawrence quits the Style Boyz for a farm in Colorado and his woodwork

Chargrilled rump with green chimichurri, smoky potatoes and a tomato and onion salad. Chop the parsley, oregano, garlic and chilli and mix with the vinegar, 80ml of the oil and salt. Halve the potatoes, toss with 2 tbsp of the oil, the paprika and salt and roast at 220C for 35 minutes. Rub the steak with the rest of the oil and salt and chargrill for 4 minutes a side, then rest for 8 minutes. Slice the tomatoes and onion thinly and season. Slice the steak, spoon over the chimichurri and serve with the potatoes and salad.
Smashed beef patties, cheese, onions and pickles on brioche buns

Little beef patties with melted cheddar, pickles, caramelised onion and burger sauce in soft brioche slider buns, eaten with one hand. Slowly fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp mustard and 1 tbsp chopped pickles. Roll 600g beef mince into 12 balls, smash flat in a very hot oiled pan, season and cook 2 minutes. Flip, add half a cheese slice each and cook 1 minute. Toast 12 brioche slider buns and fill with sauce, patty, onions and pickles.
Mary from HR's approved roast salmon
Mary from HR has signed off on it, and it is strictly non-denominational

Side of salmon roasted with honey mustard and dill, with crushed potatoes and green beans. Boil the potatoes for 18 minutes, drain and crush with the oil and salt. Mix the mustard, honey, lemon zest and half the chopped dill. Lay the salmon on a lined tray, spread with the glaze and roast at 200C for 15 minutes. Boil the beans for 4 minutes and toss with the butter. Scatter the salmon with the rest of the dill and serve with lemon wedges, potatoes and beans.
Linguine with garlic butter prawns and crunchy toasted breadcrumbs

Linguine tossed with garlic butter king prawns, chilli, white wine, lemon and parsley, finished with toasted breadcrumbs for crunch. Cook 400g linguine in salted water. Toast 40g panko in 1 tbsp oil until golden. Heat 40g butter and 2 tbsp oil, add 4 sliced garlic cloves and 1/2 tsp chilli flakes for 1 minute, then add 600g peeled green prawns and cook 2 minutes. Add 100ml white wine and bubble 1 minute. Toss in the drained pasta with a splash of pasta water, the zest and juice of 1 lemon and chopped parsley. Top with the crumbs.
Laura's record label party short ribs
Laura caters Jensen's New Year's Eve party for the record label, and runs into him

Beef short ribs braised in red wine until falling apart, over soft parmesan polenta with gremolata. Heat the oven to 160C. Season the ribs and brown well in the oil in a heavy pot. Lift out. Fry the chopped onion, carrots and garlic for 5 minutes, stir in the tomato paste, then add the wine and stock and put the ribs back. Cover and braise in the oven for 3 hours until the meat falls off the bone. Bring the milk to the boil, whisk in the polenta and stir for 5 minutes, then beat in the parmesan and butter. Chop the parsley with the lemon zest and a little garlic for gremolata. Serve the ribs and sauce over the polenta with gremolata on top.
Rainbow Records Sunday fried chicken with baked mac and cheese
the new label's Sunday dinner the week the first record takes off

Buttermilk-soaked chicken in a crisp spiced coating, fried deep golden, with baked cheddar macaroni and a crunchy crumb top. Whisk 500ml buttermilk, 2 tbsp hot sauce and 1 tsp salt and turn 1.5kg chicken thighs and drumsticks through it. Marinate in the fridge for 4 hours. Boil 300g macaroni until just tender. Melt 40g butter, stir in 3 tbsp flour and whisk in 600ml milk until thick, then stir in most of 250g grated vintage cheddar and 1 tsp mustard powder and fold through the pasta. Top with the rest of the cheese and 50g breadcrumbs and bake at 180C for 25 minutes. Meanwhile heat 1.5 litres of oil to 165C. Mix 250g plain flour with 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp each garlic powder, cayenne and black pepper and 1 tsp salt. Press the chicken into the flour and fry in batches for 12 to 14 minutes until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack for 5 minutes and serve with the mac and cheese.
Curtis, the Cadillac dealer who bankrolls the first record and never lets go

Pan-fried pork chops smothered in onion gravy with garlicky collard greens. Season the chops, dust in half the flour mixed with the paprika and brown in the oil for 3 minutes a side. Lift out. Fry the sliced onions in the same pan for 8 minutes until soft, stir in the rest of the flour, then whisk in the stock. Put the chops back with the thyme, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until tender in a thick gravy. Fry the sliced garlic in a little oil, add the shredded greens and a splash of water and cook for 6 minutes, then add the vinegar. Serve the chops smothered in gravy with the greens.
The seventies dinner party at the big house in the hills
The dinner party star of 1970s Hollywood: seared strips of rump in a paprika, mustard and sour cream sauce with mushrooms, over buttered egg noodles.
Bernie, the farm boy from Lincolnshire who writes every word Reggie sings

Crumbed chicken breast filled with garlic and parsley butter, with buttered peas and mash. Mash the butter with the crushed garlic and chopped parsley, roll into a log in baking paper and freeze for 20 minutes. Cut a deep pocket in each breast, push in a slice of the butter and press closed. Dip in flour, egg and panko, twice. Brown in the oil for 2 minutes a side, then bake at 200C for 20 minutes. Boil the peeled potatoes for 20 minutes and mash with milk and salt. Cook the peas for 3 minutes. Serve the Kievs with the mash and peas, butter running out.
Smoky chipotle lime chicken thighs in warm tortillas

Chipotle and lime chicken thighs chargrilled and sliced into soft tortillas with smashed avocado, pickled red onion, coriander and a squeeze of lime. Mix 2 tbsp chipotle in adobo, 2 crushed garlic cloves, the juice of 1 lime, 1 tsp cumin and 2 tbsp oil. Marinate 800g chicken thigh fillets for 30 minutes. Slice 1 red onion thin and soak in lime juice and salt for 20 minutes. Grill the chicken on a hot barbecue for 5 minutes a side and slice. Mash 2 avocados with lime and salt. Warm 12 small tortillas and fill with avocado, chicken, onion and coriander.
Kamehl Zadir, the club owner who finally waves the Butabi brothers past the rope

Grilled lamb and onion kebabs with saffron rice, charred tomatoes and yoghurt with herbs. Grate the onion, squeeze out the juice and mix with the lamb, turmeric and salt until sticky. Shape around 8 flat skewers. Soak the saffron in 2 tbsp hot water. Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, rest for 5, then stir through the saffron and butter. Grill the kebabs and halved tomatoes on a hot grill for 5 minutes a side. Mix the yoghurt with chopped mint and salt. Dust the kebabs with sumac and serve on the rice with the tomatoes, yoghurt and parsley.
Buttermilk fried chicken with mashed potatoes and pepper gravy

Chicken pieces soaked in hot sauce buttermilk, fried crackling crisp, with creamy mashed potatoes and peppery cream gravy. Soak 1.2kg chicken pieces overnight in 300ml buttermilk with 1 tbsp hot sauce and 2 tsp salt. Dredge in 250g plain flour mixed with 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp pepper. Fry at 160C for 12 to 15 minutes until 75C inside. Mash 1kg potatoes with 60g butter and 100ml milk. For gravy, whisk 2 tbsp frying oil with 2 tbsp flour, then 400ml milk, simmer until thick and season with lots of pepper.
the trip to India with the Beatles, where it all goes very colourful

Pumpkin, cauliflower and chickpea curry with coconut, spinach, basmati rice and mango chutney. Fry the chopped onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 6 minutes, then the curry paste for 1 minute. Add the diced pumpkin, cauliflower florets, chickpeas, coconut milk and 200ml water and simmer for 25 minutes until tender. Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5. Stir the spinach through the curry until wilted. Serve with the rice, mango chutney and coriander.
Holly's in-flight chicken in white wine
the dinner service on Holly's flight, circling Dulles with the fuel running low

Chicken thighs braised with white wine, mushrooms and tarragon cream, with buttered rice and green beans. Season the chicken and brown in the butter. Lift out. Fry the sliced shallots and mushrooms for 5 minutes, then add the wine and bubble for 1 minute. Add the stock, put the chicken back and simmer for 20 minutes. Stir in the cream and chopped tarragon for the last 3 minutes. Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5. Boil the beans for 4 minutes and serve with the chicken and rice.
Slow braised beef chuck and mince with tomatoes and kidney beans, sour cream

Beef chuck and mince browned, braised 2.5 hours with onion, chilli, cumin, tomato and kidney beans. Brown 600g diced beef chuck and 400g mince. Add 1 onion, 2 tbsp chilli powder and 1 tsp cumin, then 2 tins tomatoes. Braise 2.5 hours, adding 2 tins kidney beans for the last 30 minutes. Serve with sour cream and grated cheddar.
Beef goulash with sweet paprika over buttered egg noodles, sour cream on top
Beef chuck browned with onions and lots of paprika, simmered 3 hours with tomato until thick, with buttered noodles and sour cream.
Bucky buying plums at the Bucharest market the morning the whole world comes for him

Chicken thighs roasted with plums, paprika and onions over soft polenta with sour cream. Heat the oven to 200C. Rub the chicken with the paprika, crushed garlic, oil and salt. Roast the chicken on the onion wedges for 20 minutes, then add the halved plums drizzled with honey and roast for 20 minutes more. Bring the milk to the boil, whisk in the polenta and stir for 5 minutes, then beat in the butter. Serve the chicken and plums over the polenta with sour cream and dill.
Airbase rib eye, corn and slaw
Grilled rib eyes and corn on the cob with creamy cabbage slaw
Rib eye steaks grilled hot, corn on the cob, coleslaw with a creamy vinegar dressing.
Ramada cooking on Topper's stomach. We used a cast iron pan

Chilli lime chicken, capsicum and onion brought to the table sizzling, with tortillas, guacamole and sour cream. Slice the chicken into strips and toss with the cumin, paprika, juice of 2 limes, 1 tbsp of the oil and salt. Mash the avocados with the last lime and salt. Get a cast iron pan smoking hot. Cook the chicken in the rest of the oil for 6 minutes, add the sliced capsicums and onion and cook for 4 minutes more. Take the pan to the table still sizzling, with warm tortillas, guacamole, sour cream and coriander.
the Baron's birthday party at his castle in Vulgaria

Thin crumbed pork schnitzel fried golden in butter, with lemon and a warm mustard and chive potato salad. Boil 800g kipfler potatoes until tender. Warm 125ml vegetable stock with 2 tbsp white wine vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon mustard and 1 finely chopped small red onion, slice the potatoes hot, pour over the dressing, add 3 tbsp oil and chopped chives and season. Pound 600g pork loin steaks to 5mm between baking paper and season. Dip in 75g plain flour, 2 beaten eggs and 150g dry breadcrumbs. Fry in 150ml oil and 30g butter over medium high heat for 2 to 3 minutes a side until golden. Serve with lemon wedges and the warm potato salad.
Lord Scrumptious's roast beef and Yorkshires
Truly's father, the sweet factory lord who won't buy the Toot Sweets

Roast sirloin with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes, gravy and horseradish cream. Whisk 120g of the flour, the eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and leave to stand. Heat the oven to 220C. Rub the beef with 1 tbsp of the oil and salt and roast for 45 minutes for medium rare, with the parboiled potatoes in 1 tbsp of oil on another tray. Rest the beef. Turn the oven to 230C, put a drop of the rest of the oil in a 12-hole muffin tin and heat for 5 minutes, fill with batter and bake for 18 minutes until puffed. Stir the rest of the flour into the beef pan, whisk in the stock and simmer for 4 minutes for gravy. Whip the cream softly and fold in the horseradish. Carve and serve with the Yorkshires, potatoes, gravy and horseradish cream.
the hot dinner service on the overnight route to Paris

Season the chicken with the salt and pepper and brown skin side down in the oil in a wide heavy pan, then turn, brown and lift out. Fry the bacon, onions and mushrooms in the same pan until golden, then add the garlic. Stir in the flour and tomato paste, pour in 500ml red wine and 250ml chicken stock, and add the thyme and bay. Return the chicken skin side up, cover and simmer gently. Uncover and simmer until the sauce coats a spoon. Scatter with parsley and serve with torn baguette.
the other choice on the dinner trolley, for the passengers who stayed on Flight 180

Salmon baked in a paper parcel with fennel, lemon, dill and butter, with herbed rice. Heat the oven to 200C. Slice the fennel, zucchini and 1 lemon thinly. Lay each salmon fillet on a sheet of baking paper on a bed of fennel and zucchini, top with lemon, dill and butter, season and fold into a tight parcel. Bake on a tray for 15 minutes. Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, rest for 5, then stir through chopped parsley and the juice of the other lemon. Open the parcels at the table and serve with the rice.
Sydney Harbour barramundi with salsa verde
a harbourside dinner from the Sydney leg of the mission
Crisp-skinned barramundi fillets on crushed lemon potatoes with a sharp salsa verde of parsley, mint, capers, garlic and lemon.
Ambrose's hideout in the old fort on Bare Island, out in Botany Bay

Rosemary and garlic lamb rack with crushed potatoes, minted peas and red wine jus. Boil the potatoes for 18 minutes, drain and crush with a little oil. Rub the lamb with chopped rosemary, garlic, oil and salt, sear fat side down, then roast at 200C for 20 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes. Pour the wine into the roasting pan, bubble on the stove, add the stock and reduce for 5 minutes. Cook the peas for 3 minutes and crush with the butter and chopped mint. Cut into cutlets and serve on the potatoes and peas with the jus.
Weyland's money buys the good fillet, even this far from Earth

Season an 800g centre-cut eye fillet and sear all over in oil, then brush with 2 tbsp Dijon. Blitz 500g mushrooms and 2 garlic cloves and cook in 25g butter with thyme until dry. Cool both. Lay 8 slices prosciutto on cling film, spread with the mushrooms, roll the beef up tight and chill 20 minutes. Wrap in 2 sheets puff pastry, brush with egg, score and bake at 210C for 35 minutes for medium rare. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
David, alone on the ship for two years, bleaching his hair to look like Peter O'Toole

Spiced roast chicken with jewelled rice of pistachios, barberries or cranberries, and herbs, with garlic yoghurt. Rub the chicken with the baharat, oil, lemon juice and salt and roast at 200C for 40 minutes until crisp. Soak the saffron in 2 tbsp hot water. Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, rest for 5, then stir through the saffron and butter. Fold the chopped pistachios, cranberries and parsley through the rice. Mix the yoghurt with the crushed garlic and a pinch of salt. Serve the chicken on the jewelled rice with the garlic yoghurt.
Seared rump, Swiss cheese, jammy onions, rocket and mustard mayo

Thin seared rump on toasted Turkish bread with caramelised onions, melted Swiss cheese, rocket, tomato and hot English mustard mayo. Slowly fry 3 sliced onions in 30g butter and 1 tbsp brown sugar for 20 minutes until jammy. Bat 4 rump steaks to 1cm thick, season and sear in a very hot pan for 1 minute a side. Lay a slice of Swiss cheese on each and cover for 30 seconds to melt. Toast 4 halved Turkish rolls. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise with 2 tsp hot English mustard. Build each with mayo, rocket, tomato, steak and onions. Make two each.
Gail Stanwyk's country club Cobb salad
Gail at the club in her tennis whites, while Fletch puts lunch on the Underhills' tab

Grilled chicken, crisp bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese in rows over cos with a red wine vinaigrette. Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and peel. Cook the chicken in a hot grill pan for 5 minutes a side, rest and dice. Fry the bacon until crisp and break up. Shake the vinegar, mustard, oil and salt in a jar. Chop the cos onto a platter and lay rows of chicken, bacon, chopped egg, avocado, halved tomatoes and crumbled blue cheese across the top. Scatter with chives and pour over the dressing at the table.
Workhouse governors' roast chicken and bread sauce
What the board eats at the top table while the boys queue for gruel
The feast the workhouse board keep for themselves: golden roast chicken with lemon and thyme, crisp roast potatoes and carrots, peas and a proper clove-scented bread sauce.
Nancy leading Oom-Pah-Pah round the tables at the Three Cripples

Beef and onion pies in shortcrust with mash and green parsley liquor. Toss the beef in 1 tbsp of the flour and brown in the oil. Add the sliced onions for 5 minutes. Add the stock and Worcestershire, cover and simmer for 1 and a half hours until tender and thick. Cool. Line four pie tins with shortcrust, fill, top with puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 30 minutes. Boil the peeled potatoes for 20 minutes and mash with half the butter and a splash of the milk. Melt the rest of the butter, stir in the rest of the flour, whisk in the rest of the milk and simmer for 3 minutes, then blend with the parsley and vinegar for the liquor. Serve each pie with a scoop of mash and the liquor poured over.
the dish Rocky tells his stories over, table by table

Pound 4 thin slices beef topside (600g). Mix 60g pecorino, 40g breadcrumbs, 2 garlic cloves, a handful of parsley and 30g pine nuts. Lay prosciutto on each slice, spread with the filling, roll and tie. Brown in oil, soften 1 onion, add 1.4 litres passata and basil and simmer the rolls covered for 1 and a half hours. Cook 200g polenta in 1 litre water with 40g butter and 40g parmesan. Slice the braciole and serve over polenta with the gravy.
Adrian's own recipe, the way she cooked it on Tusculum Street

Chicken braised with tomato, capsicum, mushrooms, olives and rosemary, with crusty bread. Season the chicken and brown skin side down in the oil. Lift out. Fry the sliced onion, capsicum, mushrooms and garlic for 6 minutes. Add the tomatoes and rosemary, put the chicken back skin side up and simmer, half covered, for 35 minutes. Stir in the olives, scatter with parsley and serve with torn bread.
college town cooking from Sidney's new home in Ohio
Cinnamon and clove spiced beef chilli simmered thin and slow, ladled over spaghetti and buried under kidney beans, raw onion and a mound of finely grated cheddar.
Sidney as Cassandra in the college's Greek tragedy, with a chorus in masks

Lemon and oregano chicken skewers with warm pita, tzatziki and a tomato, cucumber and feta salad. Cut the chicken into chunks and toss with the juice of 1 lemon, the oregano, 2 crushed garlic cloves, half the oil and salt. Thread onto skewers. Grate half the cucumber, squeeze it out and mix with the yoghurt, the last garlic clove and salt. Chop the tomatoes, the rest of the cucumber and the onion, top with feta and dress with the rest of the oil and lemon. Grill the skewers on a hot grill for 10 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through. Warm the pita and serve with the skewers, tzatziki and salad.
a hot dinner on the table at 284 Green Street before the lights go out

Lamb mince braised with carrot, celery and thyme, peas through it, under buttery mash with a cheddar crust. Cook 1 diced brown onion, 2 diced carrots and 2 diced celery sticks in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft. Turn up the heat, add 800g lamb mince and brown it well. Stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste and 2 tbsp plain flour, then 500ml beef stock, 1 tbsp worcestershire sauce and 1 tsp dried thyme, and simmer for 30 minutes until thick. Meanwhile boil 1.2kg floury potatoes until tender and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk, then season. Stir 150g frozen peas through the mince, season and tip into a 2 litre baking dish. Spread the mash on top, rough it up with a fork, scatter with 60g grated cheddar and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Maurice Grosse's Friday fish and chips
Maurice, the investigator with the tape recorder, brings tea home wrapped in newspaper

Beer-battered flathead with thick chips, mushy peas, tartare and malt vinegar. Bake the chips at 220C for 25 minutes. Cook the peas for 4 minutes, drain and crush with the butter, chopped mint and salt. Mix the mayonnaise with the chopped capers and a squeeze of lemon. Whisk 120g of the flour with the baking powder and lager until smooth. Heat the oil to 180C. Dust the fish in the rest of the flour, dip in the batter and fry in batches for 4 minutes until golden. Serve with the chips, mushy peas, tartare, lemon and malt vinegar.
grilled down by the InGen docks in San Diego

Blend the juice of 1 orange and 2 limes, 4 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chilli powder, 3 tbsp oil and a handful of coriander and marinate 800g skirt steak for 2 hours. Char 4 tomatoes, half a white onion and 1 jalapeño in a dry pan and blitz with coriander, lime and salt. Grill the steak over high heat for 4 minutes a side, rest 10 minutes and slice across the grain. Serve with 12 warm corn tortillas, sliced avocado and the salsa.
Roland Tembo's hunters' camp chicken curry
the great white hunter who only came to Isla Sorna for the buck rex

Chicken, potato and tomato curry cooked over the camp stove, with rice, chapati and lime pickle. Fry the sliced onions in the oil for 8 minutes, then the grated garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute. Add the diced chicken, diced potato, tomatoes and 250ml water and simmer for 30 minutes until the potato is tender. Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5. Warm the chapati in a dry pan. Scatter the curry with coriander and serve with rice, chapati and lime pickle.
Garlic butter sirloin with oven fries and creamed spinach
New York strip steaks seared hard in a cast-iron pan with garlic butter, sliced and served with fries and creamed spinach.
Champ Kind's Chicken of the Cave
Champ swears it's chicken. It's chicken here, we checked

Buttermilk fried chicken with hot honey, pickles and a crunchy cabbage slaw. Soak the chicken in the buttermilk with half the paprika and salt for at least 20 minutes. Mix the flour with the rest of the paprika, the garlic powder and salt. Toss the chicken in it, pressing to coat. Heat the oil to 170C and fry in batches for 6 to 7 minutes until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack. Warm the honey with the chilli flakes. Toss the shredded cabbage with the mayonnaise and salt and serve with the chicken, hot honey and pickles.

S: Annie lost her licence for speeding, which is why she's on the bus at all

Chargrilled corn with lime mayo, cotija, chilli and coriander. Brush the corn with melted butter and cook in a very hot grill pan, turning, for 10 minutes until charred all over. Mix the mayonnaise with the zest and juice of 1 lime. Brush the hot corn with the lime mayo, roll in crumbled cotija, dust with chilli and scatter with coriander. Serve with lime wedges.
Corn chips baked with black beans, melted cheddar and sliced jalapeños

Corn chips layered with cheddar, jalapeños and black beans, baked at 200C for 8 minutes, then sour cream and salsa. Spread a 300g bag of corn chips on a tray. Scatter over a drained tin of black beans, 200g grated cheddar and sliced jalapeños. Bake at 200C for 8 minutes until melted. Top with sour cream and a jar of salsa.
Smoky buttered pretzels and peanuts, baked and bagged for the ride
Toss 200g hard pretzels and 200g roasted peanuts with 50g melted butter and 1 tsp smoked paprika. Spread on a tray and bake at 160C for 15 minutes, stirring once. Cool and tip into paper bags.
M: Grilled lime and orange marinated skirt steak in double corn tortillas, salsa verde
Carne asada: skirt steak marinated in lime, orange, garlic and cumin, grilled hot, chopped, in doubled corn tortillas with onion, coriander and salsa verde.
Pop quiz, hotshot. Harry's line, before the elevator job goes sideways

Crumbed chicken thigh burgers with slaw, pickles and chipotle mayo on toasted brioche. Flatten the chicken, then dip in flour, beaten egg and panko. Shallow fry in the oil for 4 minutes a side until golden and cooked through. Mix half the mayonnaise with the chopped chipotle. Toss the shredded cabbage with the rest and the lime juice. Toast the buns, spread with chipotle mayo and fill with chicken, slaw and pickles.
Hideout cabin salmon with dill butter
Salmon baked in foil with dill butter, crushed potatoes, charred beans

Salmon fillets baked in foil parcels with lemon and dill butter, served with crushed garlic potatoes and charred green beans. Mash 60g soft butter with 2 tbsp chopped dill, the zest of 1 lemon and 1 crushed garlic clove. Boil 800g baby potatoes for 15 minutes, drain, crush lightly and toss with 2 tbsp olive oil and salt. Lay 4 salmon fillets on squares of foil, top each with a slice of the butter and a lemon slice, then seal. Bake at 200C for 12 minutes. Fry 300g green beans in a hot pan with a splash of oil for 4 minutes until charred.
Drake, the jumpy vet up the mountain who thinks the trees are talking

Slow-cooked beef chilli with beans and smoky chipotle, cornbread and sour cream. Brown the beef in the oil in batches, then fry the chopped onion and garlic with the cumin for 5 minutes. Add the chipotle, tomatoes and 250ml water, cover and simmer for 1 and a half hours until the beef falls apart. Stir in the beans for the last 15 minutes. Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt with the buttermilk, egg and melted butter and bake in a hot greased tin at 200C for 20 minutes. Serve the chilli with wedges of cornbread and sour cream.
the dinner where Bond should have watched the wine order

Boil 600g new potatoes until tender and blanch 250g green beans. Season 600g sole fillets, dust with flour and fry in 2 tbsp oil and 20g butter for 2 minutes a side. Brown 80g butter until nutty, add the juice of a lemon, a tbsp of capers and parsley and spoon over the fish. Serve with the potatoes, beans and lemon wedges.
Kerim Bey's camp supper lamb shish
the night at the camp outside Istanbul, before the shooting starts

Chargrilled lamb, capsicum and onion skewers with bulgur pilaf, yoghurt and a shepherd's salad. Toss the lamb with the paprika, cumin, 2 tbsp of the oil, half the lemon juice and salt. Thread onto skewers with chunks of capsicum and onion. Fry the bulgur in the butter for 1 minute, add 500ml water and salt, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then rest for 5. Dice the tomatoes and cucumber and mix with chopped parsley, the rest of the oil and lemon. Grill the skewers on a very hot grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until charred. Serve on the pilaf with yoghurt and the salad.
a Dubai dinner from the night of the sandstorm
Emirati spiced rice cooked in a rich lamb broth with dried lime, cardamom, cinnamon and tomato, topped with tender lamb, fried onion, sultanas and almonds.
Benji's first job in the field, walking into the Kremlin behind a screen

Mixed mushrooms in a paprika and sour cream sauce over buttered egg noodles with dill pickles. Brown the sliced mushrooms in half the butter in batches and lift out. Fry the sliced onion and garlic in the rest of the butter for 5 minutes, then stir in the paprika and flour. Add the stock and mustard, put the mushrooms back and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the sour cream off the heat. Cook the noodles, drain and toss with a little butter. Serve over the noodles with dill and pickles on the side.
Trainman's dining car chicken and leek pie
the only hot meal running between two worlds

Brown 800g diced chicken thigh in oil, then soften 2 sliced leeks and 2 garlic cloves in 30g butter. Stir in 2 tbsp flour, then 400ml chicken stock, 150ml cream, 1 tbsp dijon and a tsp of thyme, return the chicken and simmer for 20 minutes. Cool, spoon into a pie dish, top with puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 30 minutes.

Rama-Kandra, the program who broke every rule to get his daughter out

Golden red lentil and spinach dal with a sizzling cumin and chilli tarka, basmati rice and naan. Simmer the rinsed lentils with the turmeric and 1 litre of water for 20 minutes until soft, stirring now and then. Fry the chopped onion, garlic and ginger in half the ghee for 8 minutes, add the tomatoes and stir into the lentils with the spinach. Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5. Sizzle the cumin seeds and chillies in the rest of the ghee for 1 minute and pour over the dal. Warm the naan and serve with the dal, rice, lemon and coriander.

Crispy buttermilk chicken in toasted buns with lettuce, tomato, pickles and comeback sauce. Soak the chicken in the buttermilk with salt for at least 15 minutes. Toss in the flour mixed with the paprika and fry in the oil at 170C for 7 minutes until golden and cooked through. Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce and hot sauce for the comeback sauce. Toast the buns and fill with lettuce, tomato, chicken, pickles and sauce.

Hot dogs with cheddar sauce, corn relish and crispy onions

Grilled frankfurts in toasted buns loaded with cheesy sauce, crispy fried onions, sweet corn relish and a squeeze of tomato sauce. Simmer 8 frankfurts for 5 minutes, then grill 2 minutes until marked. Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp flour, whisk in 200ml milk and simmer until thick, then stir in 100g grated cheddar. Mix 200g drained corn kernels with 2 tbsp tomato relish. Toast 8 hot dog buns and fill with frankfurts, cheese sauce, corn relish and tomato sauce, then top with 4 tbsp crispy fried onions.

Garlic and rosemary roast lamb leg with honey roast carrots, crisp potatoes and mint sauce. Heat the oven to 200C. Cut small slits in the lamb and push in garlic slivers and rosemary. Rub with 1 tbsp of the oil and salt. Roast the lamb for 1 and a half hours, with the parboiled potatoes in 1 tbsp of the oil on another tray. Toss the carrots with the rest of the oil and the honey and roast for the last 30 minutes. Chop the mint and mix with the vinegar, sugar and 2 tbsp boiling water. Rest the lamb for 15 minutes, carve and serve with the vegetables and mint sauce.
Easter Sunday roast lamb with mint sauce
Garlic rosemary roast lamb leg, roast potatoes, peas, mint sauce

Garlic and rosemary studded roast leg of lamb with crunchy roast potatoes, peas with butter and a sharp fresh mint sauce. Make small cuts all over a 2kg lamb leg and push in slivers of 4 garlic cloves and rosemary sprigs. Rub with oil and salt and roast at 190C for 1 hour 30 minutes for medium. Rest 20 minutes. Roast 1.2kg parboiled potatoes in oil alongside. For mint sauce, chop a bunch of mint with 1 tbsp sugar, add 3 tbsp boiling water and 4 tbsp malt vinegar. Serve with 300g buttered peas.

Chicken, mushrooms and capsicum in a sherry cream sauce, spooned into puff pastry shells with buttered peas. Dice the chicken and cook in half the butter for 6 minutes. Lift out. Fry the sliced mushrooms and diced capsicum in the rest of the butter for 5 minutes, then stir in the flour. Whisk in the stock, cream and sherry and simmer for 5 minutes. Put the chicken back, take off the heat and stir in the egg yolk. Warm the pastry cases at 180C for 5 minutes. Cook the peas for 3 minutes. Spoon the chicken into the cases, scatter with parsley and serve with the peas.
